mark.12.p1.b2.text: He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower.

mark.12.p1.b3.text: Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

mark.12.p2.b1.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

mark.12.p2.b2.text: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

mark.12.p2.b3.text: They struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.

mark.12.p2.b4.text: He sent still another, and this one they killed.

mark.12.p3.b1.text: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them.

mark.12.p3.b3.text: This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.

mark.12.p3.b4.text: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

mark.12.p4.b1.text: What then will the owner of the vineyard do?

mark.12.p4.b2.text: He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.

mark.12.p4.b3.text: The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

mark.12.p4.b4.text: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd,

mark.12.p5.b1.text: Later, they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words.

mark.12.p5.b2.text: Teacher, … we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one.

mark.12.p5.b3.text: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?

mark.12.p5.b4.text: Should we pay them or not?

mark.12.p6.b1.text: Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.

mark.12.p6.b2.text: Whose image is this? And whose inscription?

mark.12.p6.b4.text: Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.

mark.12.p7.b1.text: The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection,

mark.12.p7.b2.text: Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.

mark.12.p7.b3.text: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.

mark.12.p7.b4.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be?

mark.12.p8.b1.text: Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?

mark.12.p8.b2.text: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

mark.12.p9.b1.text: But concerning the dead rising, have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses,

mark.12.p9.b2.text: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob

mark.12.p9.b3.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.

mark.12.p10.b1.text: Which commandment is the most important of all?

mark.12.p10.b2.text: Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.

mark.12.p10.b3.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.

mark.12.p10.b4.text: The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other commandment is greater than these.

mark.12.p11.b1.text: Right, Teacher, … You have stated correctly that God is One

mark.12.p11.b2.text: And to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself, which is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.

mark.12.p11.b3.text: You are not far from the kingdom of God.

mark.12.p11.b4.text: And no one dared to question Him any further.

mark.12.p12.b1.text: How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?

mark.12.p12.b2.text: The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”

mark.12.p12.b3.text: David himself calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?

mark.12.p12.b4.text: And the large crowd listened to Him with delight.

mark.12.p13.b1.text: Watch out for the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, to receive greetings in the marketplaces,

mark.12.p13.b2.text: And to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.

mark.12.p13.b3.text: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers.

mark.12.p13.b4.text: These men will receive greater condemnation.

mark.12.p14.b1.text: As Jesus was sitting opposite the treasury, He watched the crowd putting money into it.

mark.12.p14.b2.text: And many rich people put in large amounts.

mark.12.p14.b3.text: Then one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which amounted to a small fraction of a denarius.

mark.12.p15.b1.text: Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.

mark.12.p15.b2.text: For they all contributed out of their surplus,

mark.12.p15.b3.text: But she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.
